title: Atlas Event
description: One record in a run's append-only log, written when the thing happens rather than when the run ends. The run document says where a run ended up; it cannot say what happened on the way, and it cannot say it while the run is still happening. Every field is the core's: a log a producer could write would be a log of what it said it did. A call is recorded as TWO events joined by `call_id` — `call_started` and `call_finished` — because that is the only way a reader can tell a call that never began from one that began and whose outcome nobody recorded. The second is the state that matters: a crash between issuing a request and receiving the answer leaves a call that may already have had every effect it was going to have, and calling that `failed` would invite a retry that repeats a side effect. There is no `unknown` outcome, because `unknown` is not something anything reports — it is what a missing `call_finished` means.

event_id.description: The run and the position, which together are what identifies an event. Derived, never supplied.

sequence.description: Position in the run's log, assigned by the log and starting at 0. A caller that could choose it could write an event before one already recorded, which is the one thing an append-only log promises cannot happen.

iteration.description: 0 before the first pass begins — a run that stopped during setup has events and no iterations.

recorded_at.description: ISO 8601, when the event was appended.

call_id.description: Present on `call_started` and `call_finished` and null on every other kind, so an unpaired call is visible rather than merely likely. Issued by the log when the call starts, so a call cannot be finished that was never started under that name.

payload.description: Everything specific to the kind. A dict rather than one flat record with mostly-null columns, because a field that is null for six of seven kinds teaches a reader nothing. Masked by `redact_document` before it is written: this file persists whether or not anyone exports the run, and a source's bytes reach it the same way they reach the run document. `call_started` carries `call_kind`, `target` and `input_sha256` — the digest, never the input, so a replay can be compared against what was sent without the input being kept. `call_finished` carries `outcome` (`ok`, `denied` or `failed`) and `error`. An `observation_recorded` event for a source already recorded is a NEW event appended after the old one, never a replacement: a source that changed under a run is something the log shows rather than something it hides. `approval_recorded` carries `decision` (`requested`, `granted`, `refused`, `consumed` or `rejected`), `approval_id`, `operation_sha256`, `operation_kind`, `tool`, `repo`, `ref` and `head`, plus `granted_by`, `expires_at` or `reason` where they apply. It never carries the token. `run_stopped` also carries `usage` (`model_calls`, `tool_calls`, `tokens`, `output_bytes`; null on an unbudgeted run) and `decision_recorded` carries `citation_verdicts`, a count per verdict and never the claims. `write_verified` carries `verified`, each post-action check's `name` and `passed`, the `ref` and `commit` written, and `rolled_back` (null when no rollback was needed).
